summary: Independently verified candidate commit 3372815f64ea6dd9f3de99742ac3101fc72dbb0c. The prepared base reproduced the reported mismatch for DeepseekV3ForCausalLM, GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM, and GptOssForCausalLM: the resolved enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion flag remained false while an enablement log was emitted. The candidate gates both affected log sites on the resolved flag without changing the intentionally disabled auto-enable policy. Its regression fails against the base implementation and passes against the exact candidate, and an independent 48-case decision matrix found no counterexamples. This fully resolves the original issue's stated contract because that issue explicitly permits gating the misleading log instead of restoring automatic enablement.

gpu_execution.evidence: The review exercised the real ROCm-aware Python resolution and hook paths, but did not launch a GPU kernel. Device discovery showed one MI350X gfx950, whereas the report environment was eight MI300X gfx942 GPUs. Distributed AITER all-reduce execution was outside the diagnostic contract and could not be reproduced on the assigned single GPU.

remaining_limitations: The assigned architecture was one MI350X (gfx950), not the reported eight MI300X (gfx942) system, so multi-rank AITER all-reduce correctness and performance remain unverified.

The candidate fixes misleading diagnostics and does not restore automatic fusion enablement. That is a complete resolution under the original issue's explicit either/or request, but it is not evidence that broad auto-enable is safe.
No native code changed, repository-environment.json lists native as null, and all changed runtime code is Python; therefore no native rebuild was applicable.

The 753B GLM-5.3 checkpoint was not available or launched. The reported model's current SGLang hook architecture, GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM (a DeepseekV2ForCausalLM subclass), was exercised through the actual argument-resolution path.
